unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Orthorectified surface reflectance as scaled unitless values in six optical bands
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Use LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2 only. Optical bands are SR_B1 blue, SR_B2 green, SR_B3 red, SR_B4 near infrared, SR_B5 shortwave infrared 1, and SR_B7 shortwave infrared 2. Stored optical values have a catalog range of 1-65455; convert to surface reflectance with DN*0.0000275-0.2 before computing indices. Mask QA_PIXEL bit 0 fill, bit 1 dilated cloud, bit 3 cloud, bit 4 cloud shadow, and bit 5 snow; bit 6 marks clear conditions and bit 7 water. QA_RADSAT bits 0-4 and 6 flag saturation in optical bands 1-5 and 7. SR_ATMOS_OPACITY uses scale 0.001; values below 0.1 are generally clear, 0.1-0.3 average, and above 0.3 hazy, but the catalog recommends QA_PIXEL for cloud discrimination. Surface reflectance is produced with LEDAPS. Do not add Landsat 7, Landsat 8/9, TOA, raw DN, annual composites, or index-only products as required anchor data.

original_anchor_asset.asset_alias_policy: The admitted anchor is the paired Landsat 5 TM and Landsat 7 ETM+ Collection 2 Level-2 Tier-1 surface-reflectance family: LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2 and LANDSAT/LE07/C02/T1_L2. A paper may use one or both collections, but it must operationally process Collection 2 Level-2 Tier-1 TM/ETM+ surface reflectance and must not extend the time series with Landsat 8/9 OLI. Collection 1, Collection 2 Level-1 DN or TOA products, Tier-2 products, annual precomputed composites and index-only collections are excluded. Level-1 raw scenes are excluded to keep the task separate from single_dataset/task_009; Landsat 8/9 OLI is excluded to keep it separate from single_dataset/task_018, single_dataset/task_019, single_dataset/task_027, single_dataset/task_028, single_dataset/task_035 and single_dataset/task_042 anchor families.
original_anchor_asset.alias_policy_scope: The supplied Methods identify TM/ETM+ LEDAPS surface reflectance but do not state the collection number. Collection 2 Level-2 Tier-1 is the ready catalog representation selected for scoring. Exact membership of the source scenes in Collection 2 remains unresolved; candidate papers must nevertheless satisfy the current exact-asset gate.

repointed_from.why_the_former_anchor_was_wrong: The source explicitly uses Landsat 5 TM and Landsat 7 ETM+ surface-reflectance scenes from 1992-2016 and does not use Landsat 8 OLI. LC08 begins in 2013 and cannot supply the 1992-2012 portion, so both sensor identity and temporal feasibility were wrong.
repointed_from.why_this_asset: The LT05 and LE07 Collection 2 Level-2 Tier-1 collections provide the exact TM and ETM+ sensor branches, 30 m orthorectified surface reflectance, 16-day revisit metadata and LEDAPS processing named by the source. Their catalog intervals jointly cover the full 1992-2016 analysis period.
repointed_from.processing_version_uncertainty: The supplied Methods do not name Collection 1 or Collection 2. The C2 collections are selected because they are the ready local-catalog products matching the stated sensors, processing level and LEDAPS algorithm. This does not prove that the source downloaded C2 scenes or that C2 reflectance and QA values are numerically identical to the source archive; a source record proving Collection 1 would require reclassifying this as a catalog substitution.

directions.research_question: How have lake water extent and littoral-zone land-cover structure evolved in four major Yangtze River lakes (Taihu, Hongze, Poyang, Dongting) from 1999 to 2019, and what are the dominant pathways of land-cover transitions in these lake–shore systems under seasonal hydrological variation and human regulation?
directions.hypothesis_or_mechanism: Lake and littoral-zone systems in the middle and lower Yangtze Plain exhibit long-term structural reorganization driven by seasonal water-level fluctuations, river–lake interactions, regional precipitation changes, and human regulation. Dry-season water extent and land-cover transitions among water, mudflat, field, built-up land, and tree classes reveal pathways of littoral-zone restructuring that differ among lakes with varying degrees of hydraulic connectivity and regulation.
directions.variables_and_data_use: Landsat 5 TM (1999–2011), Landsat 7 ETM+ (2012–2013), and Landsat 8 OLI (2013–2019) Collection 2 Tier 1 Level-2 surface reflectance (BLUE, GREEN, RED, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2 bands) were processed through CCDC time-series segmentation and Random Forest classification to generate annual dry-season land-cover maps (five classes: water, built-up land, mudflat, field, tree). Dry-season water area was extracted at a fixed January–February reference date each year. Land-cover transition matrices quantified changes between 1999 and 2019 within fixed lake–littoral analysis boundaries. Field surveys (2015–2019), Google Earth imagery, GF imagery, and NASA SRTM DEM supported reference sample interpretation and validation.
directions.method_paradigm: Time-series change detection and classification using CCDC harmonic modeling of multi-sensor Landsat surface reflectance, segment-based Random Forest classification, and date-specific annual land-cover map extraction within fixed spatial boundaries. Temporal consistency achieved through long-term model fitting rather than annual image compositing.
